title: Copilot Studio: interactive MCP apps render inside agent conversations
summary: Hold: the briefing casts Power Platform data-policy coverage of the new Copilot Studio experience as unconfirmed, although Microsoft states that these policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in scoped environments. The documented paths, commands, roadmap targets and consumption-based billing are supported.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: a maker chooses a UI-enabled MCP server, and no separate app-rendering admin switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio MCP apps admin setting disable rendering tenant default enabled switch' and '"MCP apps" "admin" "render" "Copilot Studio"'; opened MCP apps and Tools-add-MCP-server. Makers add servers and tools; no separate rendering switch was documented.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No setting specifically controlling MCP app rendering independently of server tools is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCP apps" "admin" "render" "Copilot Studio"'; opened MCP apps, Tools-add-MCP-server, Manage plugins, skills, and MCP servers, and Agent Tools overview. No app-rendering-specific setting was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated an explicit tenant-level MCP apps default beyond the roadmap description.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio MCP apps admin setting disable rendering tenant default enabled switch'; read roadmap record, MCP apps, and Tools-add-MCP-server. No explicit tenant-level rendering default was stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The app-specific documentation does not identify the execution identity for app-originated tool calls and resource reads.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio MCP apps app-originated tool calls identity authentication user audit'; opened MCP apps and Tools-add-MCP-server. They describe configured connections and checks, but no app-originated-call identity rule.

claims.claim: The cited sources do not say existing agents change automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio MCP apps admin setting disable rendering tenant default enabled switch'; read roadmap, MCP apps, and Tools-add-MCP-server. They describe UI-enabled tools and maker-added servers, not an automatic migration of existing agents.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An organisation can block an MCP server at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Registry** tab.
3. Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane.

claims.claim: The beta package block operation is POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Blocking an MCP server disables all its tools.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes.

claims.claim: The block and reject APIs are beta and unsupported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to both package operations requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block API requires delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.claim: The block API takes no request body.
claims.quote: Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Individual tools are controlled at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > Enabled or Disabled toggle > Save.
claims.quote: Select the **Tools** tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an **Enabled** or **Disabled** toggle.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of the Agent 365 individual-tool toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Agent 365 MCP individual tools enabled disabled Microsoft Graph API tool policy granular' and '"copilot/admin" "tools" "disable" MCP granular'; opened package API overview and server management. Results describe UI and gateway enforcement, not an equivalent API call.

claims.claim: Tool-level granular control is rolling out.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants

claims.claim: Individual-tool control supports only specific Agent 365 registered server types and supported calling experiences.
claims.quote: The Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces the policy at runtime for supported tools and experiences that use the gateway. Don't assume the policy applies across all products or connected components.

claims.where: controls[2].api; controls[2].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{packageId}/reject rejects a pending title submission, not a registration approval or consent grant.
claims.quote: Reject a pending Copilot package title submission. This action reviews a package title and its submitted version; it doesn't reject an individual user's request.
claims.fix: Append to controls[2].note: 'Supply the matching staged submission version in the version request-body property.' Keep the existing method and path unchanged; the Governance controls prose already documents this requirement.

claims.claim: The reject call needs the title ID confirmed for submission review, not an individual request identifier.
claims.quote: Replace `{packageId}` with the title ID confirmed for reviewing the pending submission. Don't substitute an individual request identifier.

claims.claim: The matching staged submission version is supplied in the version body property.
claims.quote: The schema defines both parameters as optional. This doesn't mean that omitting `version` selects the latest or pending version. Supply the version of the staged submission you're rejecting.

claims.claim: The reject API requires CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.claim: The Power Platform data policy route through Security, Data and privacy, Data policy, New Policy, environment selection and Assign connectors reaches the connector three-dots Block control.
claims.quote:
Select the three dots (**⋮**) next to the connector, and then:
- To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select **Block**.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Classification Blocked -Connectors <connector-objects> moves specified connectors into a policy's Blocked group.
claims.quote: The name of the group to which the connectors should be added. Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.where: controls[3].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: Governance controls: paragraph beginning Tool-level control
claims.claim: Because the data-policy page does not mention MCP apps, coverage of a server added through the new Copilot Studio experience remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.
claims.fix: Replace 'The Power Platform data policy page covers Power Platform connectors used as tools and does not mention MCP apps, so confirm that a server added through the new Copilot Studio experience is covered.' with 'Power Platform data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy scope; blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers.' The cited page states both facts; do not extend the uncertainty about Agent 365 gateway enforcement to Power Platform data-policy coverage.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center manages plugins, skills and MCP servers, while Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 provides administrative controls for supported tools. Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components. An approval or block doesn't necessarily apply across all products or connected components.

claims.claim: The standard-harness MCP overview says server tool and resource changes are dynamically reflected.
claims.quote: When you update or remove tools and resources on the MCP server, Copilot Studio dynamically reflects these changes.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness how-to says to edit the server entry to refresh the connection and tool list after server changes.
claims.quote: If a server's URL, authentication, or exposed tools change after you add it, edit the server entry in the same **Tools** dialog to refresh the connection and re-read the tool list.

claims.claim: After Block, select Next, define scope if prompted, select Next and create the reviewed new policy.
claims.quote: Review your policy, and then select **Create policy** if you're creating a new policy or **Update policy** if you're editing an existing policy.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The data-policy page does not specifically mention MCP apps or a rendered-interface control.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio Microsoft Copilot harness data policies MCP servers connectors enforcement'; read Configure data policies for agents in full. It covers scoped agents and connected MCP tools, but does not mention MCP apps or a rendered-interface control.
